items.title: Father Al Lewis Interview, 1972-02-21
items.q: He was playing bass and Charlie Hamilton on piano and I was on guitar and Brady was on drums.

ctx.x: Yeah, you told me before, I can't remember who, but anyway, what about Jewel's Tavern and Dixieland Inn or something, all those places, were there a lot of joints on St. Charles around the 1300 block there?

No, they used to have one at, Melchomene, St. Charles Minor, with, Minor, B Minor was playing up there with a group but they didn't have nothing compared with what we had. Now when I was playing at the cathedral at St. Charles, I had Ollie Popper playing bass, and you know, and Brady, that's the guy I couldn't think of at the time, had Ollie Popper playing bass. And we should call him, Charles Thomas was his name, we called him Ollie Popper. He was playing bass and Charlie Hamilton on piano and I was on guitar…
And what about Magazine Street and Chappatoulas, was there anything over that way in my childhood?
